hook: SCP-1689 is a burlap sack of potatoes, and the joke is that it never runs out. The file is short and deadpan, so read the containment notes closely: the exception made for the site cooks is the first wink.
whyItMatters: It belongs to the comfortable tradition of mundane objects with bottomless insides, played here for comedy with an edge of unease; its tags include both comedy and horror. It is a neat example of how a single absurd image can be turned into the setup for an expedition, with the mission log itself kept on a separate page.
thingsToNotice: The tone shifts in the addendum about the Siberian village: a community that lived on the sack for more than a century turns out to be badly malnourished, which gives a silly premise a sad undertow. The villagers' belief that it was a reward for their labor, from a giver nobody remembers, hints at a story the file never tells. Small details build the scale, from regrowth that doubles every two hours to a special enzyme compound developed for exploring it. A proposal to set up a mobile site inside a sack of potatoes is both very funny and faintly ominous.

related.note: Another everyday interior that is far too large, played for both laughs and dread.
A food-dispensing anomaly whose humor also comes from deadpan testing.
